## When to use this skill

Use this skill when writing tests for components, setting up test infrastructure, or debugging component behavior. Covers unit testing, E2E testing, and testing best practices.

For test examples, patterns and debugging strategies, see [references/REFERENCE.md](references/REFERENCE.md).

For project-specific test setup and conventions, refer to `.context/CLAUDE.md` or `.context/COPILOT.md`.

- Prefer small test harnesses that mount the component in a JS test runner (Jest/Node DOM) if available.

## E2E with Playwright

- Install: `pnpm add -D @playwright/test`
- Typical scripts:
  - `playwright test`
  - `playwright test --headed`
- Keep tests deterministic: seed storage or mock the `storage` service.

## Example Playwright test (concept)

```javascript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('song search filters list', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('http://localhost:1234');
  await page.fill('input[data-filter]', 'love');
  const items = await page.locator('kt-song-queue ul li');
  await expect(items).toHaveCount(1);
});
```

## CI

- Add a GitHub Actions workflow to run Playwright tests in CI when present.

state.task: We have a Django 4.2 + DRF backend and a React frontend for our internal project management tool "TaskForge." I need you to help me build out a comprehensive test suite covering all layers. Specifically: (1) Write pytest tests for the REST API endpoints — projects CRUD, task assignment, and the deadline notification logic — using factory_boy fixtures and mocking our Celery beat scheduler; make sure we test auth edge cases like expired JWT tokens and permission boundaries between org admins and regular members. (2) Create a Playwright E2E test suite that covers the critical user journeys: logging in, creating a project, dragging tasks between Kanban columns (we use react-beautiful-dnd), uploading attachments, and verifying the real-time WebSocket updates when another user modifies a task. The tests should run against both Chromium and Firefox and capture screenshots on failure. (3) Set up performance profiling for our two slowest pages — the "All Projects" dashboard that loads 500+ project cards with avatar rollups, and the Gantt chart view that renders ~2,000 task bars. I want Lighthouse CI scores captured in a report, plus custom Playwright timing marks measuring time-to-interactive and largest contentful paint for both pages under throttled 3G conditions. (4) Finally, wire all of this into a single `make test-all` command that spins up the Docker Compose stack (Postgres, Redis, Django, React dev server), seeds the database with realistic fixture data, runs the pytest suite, then the Playwright E2E and perf suites in parallel where possible, and generates a unified HTML report. Include a GitHub Actions workflow YAML that runs this on every PR targeting `main`.
